extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties before the PTAB (petitioners, patent owners, counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria used by the PTAB to decide whether to institute an inter partes review, with emphasis on discretionary denial when multiple petitions and overlapping challenges exist (the General Plastic factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 314(a) reasonable likelihood requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a), the Director may not authorize an inter partes review unless the information in the petition and any response “shows that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the petition.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution requires a showing of reasonable likelihood to prevail on at least one challenged claim. However, § 314(a) does not compel institution; the Director (delegated to the Board) retains discretion to deny institution even if the statutory threshold is met (see Harmonic Inc. v. Avid Tech.).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic Factor 1: same petitioner previously filed petition directed to same claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the same petitioner previously filed a petition directed to the same claims of the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlapping petitions challenging the same claims (especially when most challenged claims overlap) weigh in favor of discretionary denial. If only a few additional claims are added and the later petition devotes little analysis to them, this factor strongly favors denying institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic Factor 2: whether petitioner knew or should have known of asserted prior art at time of first petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether at the time of filing the earlier petition the petitioner knew of the prior art asserted in the later petition or should have known of it (i.e., whether reasonable diligence would have discovered it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner should show evidence of search efforts and explain why new prior art was not found earlier. A prior art reference cited on the face of the patent (or a closely similar family member) supports a finding that a reasonably diligent searcher should have discovered related references; failure to provide testimony/evidence of diligence weighs strongly against institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic Factor 3: whether petitioner had received patent owner’s preliminary response or Board’s institution decision in prior petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, at the time of filing the second petition, the petitioner already received the patent owner’s preliminary response to the first petition or the Board’s decision on whether to institute review in the first petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a short window to review an opponent’s preliminary response can permit use of that response as a roadmap; filing a near-immediate follow-on petition after seeing a preliminary response tends to weigh in favor of denying institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic Factor 4: length of time between learning of the prior art and filing the second petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The elapsed time between when the petitioner learned of the new prior art and when it filed the subsequent petition relying on that art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short gap (e.g., 25 days) may be reasonable, but the petitioner should substantiate the timing with declarations or other evidence about discovery and preparation. Absent such proof, this factor may be treated as neutral or weigh against institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic Factor 5: adequate explanation for time elapsed between multiple petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner provides an adequate explanation for the elapsed time between filings of multiple petitions directed to the same claims of the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical early filing (e.g., filing early in the statutory period for strategic reasons) is not an adequate excuse for not completing prior-art searches; petitioners must explain why they filed early and why they could not have included the later art in the earlier petition. Anticipated shifts in asserted claims do not necessarily justify staggered filings; petitioners should challenge all claims that could plausibly be asserted or file parallel petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic Factor 6: finite resources of the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the Board’s limited resources when multiple petitions or overlapping proceedings would increase workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If instituting a second overlapping proceeding would multiply proceedings or unpatentability grounds and impose additional burden (especially where consolidation is infeasible due to differing evidentiary records), this factor weighs in favor of discretionary denial. Petitioner proposals to shorten deadlines or consolidate must be realistic about Board timing and effects on workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic Factor 7 / 35 U.S.C. § 316(a)(11): one-year final determination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board must issue a final determination not later than 1 year after the date on which the Director notices institution of review (35 U.S.C. § 316(a)(11)), and this timing obligation factors into discretionary-denial analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If instituting additional proceedings or expanding grounds would make compliance with the one-year mandate impracticable or inefficient, this factor supports denial; where petitioner can show the trial could be completed within one year, this factor may be neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to substantiate search/diligence with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner should provide evidence (declarations, testimony, or factual record) describing the manner and timing of its prior-art searches and discovery of new references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney argument alone is insufficient; submissions should include factual support showing reasonable diligence. Failure to provide such evidence undermines claims that the reference could not have been found earlier and weighs against institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prosecution history / cited references as indicator of discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: References cited on the face of the patent (e.g., in an IDS or examiner citations) or closely similar family members of cited references are indicators that related prior art was reasonably discoverable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reference in the same family (or a substantially similar reference) was cited during prosecution, a reasonably diligent searcher should have located related documents; this supports a finding that petitioner 'should have known' of the later-asserted art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and scope of new-claim analysis in follow-on petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent and depth of a petitioner’s analysis for claims newly added in a subsequent petition (e.g., number of pages devoted to new dependent claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal analysis (e.g., less than a page) for newly asserted claims suggests the petition is duplicative and may weigh against institution; petitioners should provide substantive claim-specific analysis for any new claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation feasibility / efficiency assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Board can and should consolidate overlapping proceedings and whether consolidation would reduce Board workload or be infeasible because of different evidentiary records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner’s proposal to consolidate must account for realistic scheduling and the fact that consolidation may be impractical if the proceedings rely on different primary references and distinct evidentiary records; inability to consolidate or increased total work supports discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excusing late filings under 37 C.F.R. § 42.5(c)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may excuse a late filing (e.g., a preliminary sur-reply) when consideration of the late filing is in the interests of justice, per 37 C.F.R. § 42.5(c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late filings can be excused on a showing that consideration furthers the interests of justice; the decision to excuse is discretionary and fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exhaustive nature of General Plastic factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Plastic list is explicitly non-exhaustive; additional factors may be considered where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond the enumerated factors, the Board may consider other case-specific considerations in deciding whether to exercise its discretion to deny institution under § 314(a).
